result.question: Give me a sample-by-sample picture of the fault gases in Transformer 1 at MAIN between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. For each sample, list hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Name the dominant gas, meaning the one with the highest ppm, and give its percentage of the five-gas total. Then tell me whether the dominant gas changed at any point in the window. Say what that shift points to, for example hydrogen pointing to partial discharge, ethylene to a hotter thermal fault, or acetylene to arcing. Also rank the five gases by their percentage growth from the first to the last sample. If a gas is null in a sample, leave it out of that sample's total and mark it as missing. If fewer than two samples have all five gases, give the ranking from the latest reading alone and say that no trend could be established.
result.answer:
Ethylene was the dominant gas in all four samples, so the dominant gas never changed. It pointed to a hot thermal fault the whole time, with no sign of a move toward partial discharge or arcing.

**Fault gases, Transformer 1 (MAIN), 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-18 (4 samples, no missing values)**

| Sample | H₂ (ppm) | CH₄ (ppm) | C₂H₆ (ppm) | C₂H₄ (ppm) | C₂H₂ (ppm) | 5-gas total (ppm) | Dominant gas | % of total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 2,845 | 7,406 | 5,467 | 16,684 | 7 | 32,409 | Ethylene | 51.48% |
| 2024-01-16 | 2,950 | 7,200 | 5,400 | 16,500 | 6 | 32,056 | Ethylene | 51.47% |
| 2024-01-17 | 2,800 | 7,300 | 5,500 | 16,700 | 8 | 32,308 | Ethylene | 51.69% |
| 2024-01-18 | 2,900 | 7,350 | 5,450 | 16,600 | 7 | 32,307 | Ethylene | 51.38% |

**What the gas pattern points to**
- Ethylene made up about 51–52% of the five-gas total throughout. Methane and ethane were also high, and acetylene stayed very low (6–8 ppm).
- Hydrogen stayed a minor share, so there's no sign of partial discharge. Acetylene stayed low, so there's no sign of arcing.
- The gas ratios are steady across all four samples: ethylene/ethane ≈ 3.05, methane/hydrogen ≈ 2.5, and acetylene/ethylene < 0.001. On the standard ratio method for oil gas analysis (IEC 60599 Rogers ratios), that matches a high-temperature thermal fault above roughly 700 °C, such as an overheated connection, core or winding. Because ethylene/ethane sits just above the cut-off of 3, the exact temperature band is borderline.
- The pattern is stable but the gas levels are very high, above 16,000 ppm of ethylene. This transformer needs urgent attention.

**Growth from first sample (01-15) to last sample (01-18)**

| Rank | Gas | Growth |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hydrogen | +1.93% (2,845 → 2,900) |
| 2 | Acetylene | 0.00% (7 → 7) |
| 3 | Ethane | −0.31% (5,467 → 5,450) |
| 4 | Ethylene | −0.50% (16,684 → 16,600) |
| 5 | Methane | −0.76% (7,406 → 7,350) |

All four samples had all five gases, so a trend could be worked out. Every change is within about ±2%, which looks like normal sample-to-sample scatter rather than real growth. The fault is steady at a very high level, not getting worse within this window.
